newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Stock strategists up FTSE 100 forecasts.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Stock strategists up FTSE 100 forecasts.

text.p: Year-end forecasts for the FTSE 100 index of blue-chip British stocks were being raised sharply on Monday as stock market strategists reacted to the market's record-breaking run following Labour's stunning win in the May 1 election.

After incoming finance minister Gordon Brown took markets by surprise last week when he set the Bank of England free to set interest rates, analysts said the outlook for UK shares and bonds looks much brighter.

Not only did Labour secure a greater-than-expected majority, easing political uncertainties, Brown's surprise move on monetary policy dramatically improved the UK's inflation prospects -- making the UK market more attractive.

The FTSE 100 on Monday set its seventh record close in as many sessions, ending up 38.7 points at 4,669.6 -- some 5.2 percent higher than on the eve of the poll and up 13.3 percent from its level at the end of 1996.
At HSBC James Capel, strategists raised their year-end target for the FTSE 100 to 4,800 from 4,400, citing Labour's decision to give the central bank greater freedom.
"The main reason was the independence of the Bank of England," UK equity strategist Robert Buckland said.

"It has knocked 50 basis points off our gilt forecast, and we have also factored in a relatively cautious outlook on the relationship between equities and gilts because of some concerns about a change in the dividend taxation regime."
Merrill Lynch strategists raised their year-end target to 5,000 from 4,500, in line with a reduction in bond yield targets.
But UK equity strategist Philip Wolstencroft said there were other reasons for the increased target.

"We also have other technical factors in the market which are still very strong, such as director buying," Wolstencroft said. "Over the past four weeks on a moving average basis the director buying ratio is 2.5 percent, which is a pretty strong buy," Wolstencroft said.
"We still think there is room for growth alongside the market being at its peak...because we haven't got the technical signs that outline the introduction to a bear market."
Lehman Brothers strategists raised their year-end target to 5,000 from 4,600, based on the bond yield gap, strategist Ian Scott said.
Scott said UK equities look cheaply-valued given where bond yields currently stand.
"The market is around six percent below what fair value is at the moment and we think gilt yields could still fall a bit further," he said.
UBS strategists raised to 4,600 from 4,300 while at Panmure Gordon, Ian Williams on Friday upped his forecast to 5,000 from 4,500.
Yet not everyone was rushing to jump on the bandwagon.

Steve Wright at BZW -- a member of the team voted top in last month's Reuters fund managers poll -- said BZW's 4,300 target was under review, but the brokerage retained some concerns about the UK stock market outlook.
"We are still quite concerned about the outlook for (company) earnings and taxation in the corporate sector," Wright said.

"We are concerned about the growth outlook for the UK corporate sector and think that justifies the market being on a low rating compared with other international markets...we expect gilts to continue outperforming equities."
